title: Stage 3: Config and secrets
summary: Hand the API its settings and the database password without baking them into the image.

steps.title: The API's configuration
body: password: czNjcjN0UEBzcw==    # (created by the pipeline from the vault, never committed)
valueFrom: { secretKeyRef: { name: shop-db, key: username } }
valueFrom: { secretKeyRef: { name: shop-db, key: password } }
The same Secret feeds the database: the postgres image reads `POSTGRES_USER` and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` on first start.

steps.prompt: ASP.NET Core reads `Db__Host` from the environment. Which configuration key does the app see?
steps.explain: `__` maps to `:` because `:` is not allowed in environment variable names on every platform.

buckets: Neither: leave it out of the cluster config
steps.explain: The image tag belongs in the Deployment (the template), so changing it triggers a rollout.

steps.prompt: The pipeline rotates the database password in the Secret. The API pods use `secretKeyRef` env vars. What else must happen?
options: Restart the API pods (`kubectl rollout restart deploy/shop-api`) so they read the new value, and change the password in PostgreSQL itself
steps.explain: Env vars are read at process start. The database also needs `ALTER USER`; the postgres image only uses `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` when initialising an empty data directory.

steps.title: Config in a ConfigMap, credentials in a Secret
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl`; the current namespace is `todo`, and the manifests live in `~/k8s`. `~/k8s/migrate.yaml` is the database migration Job. It reads `Db__Host` and `Db__Name` from the
ConfigMap `todo-config`, and `Db__Username` and `Db__Password` from the Secret `todo-db-credentials` (the double
underscore is how .NET reads `Db:Host` from the environment). Neither exists yet.
3. Run the Job (`kubectl apply -f ~/k8s/migrate.yaml`) and wait until it is **Complete**.

checks.name: the migration completed
checks.cmd: kubectl wait --for=condition=Complete job/todo-migrate --timeout=20s >/dev/null && kubectl logs job/todo-migrate
checks.fail: `todo-migrate` has not completed. `kubectl describe job todo-migrate` and `kubectl logs job/todo-migrate`.

checks.name: credentials are in the Secret, settings in the ConfigMap
checks.cmd: kubectl get configmap todo-config -o jsonpath='{.data}' | jq -c 'keys'; kubectl get secret todo-db-credentials -o jsonpath='{.data}' | jq -c 'keys'

hints: `kubectl apply -f ~/k8s/migrate.yaml`, then `kubectl wait --for=condition=Complete job/todo-migrate --timeout=60s`. If it failed before you created them, delete the Job and apply again.
steps.explain: Settings and credentials travel separately: the ConfigMap can be read by anyone debugging, the Secret only by whom RBAC allows, and the Job combines both with two `envFrom` sources. In the TodoApi, `builder.Configuration` turns `Db__Host` back into `Db:Host`. A migration as a Job (or an init container) runs once per release, and `kubectl wait --for=condition=Complete` is how a pipeline waits for it.
